title: Arranger versus composer; the lack of royalties
summary: Gil says he is mostly an orchestrator and arranger and woke up to the lack of royalties.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Are you happiest, or happier I should say, being a composer or an arranger or can
I haven't been much of a composer. I've been mostly an arranger you know. I haven't done much.......
So you think of yourself as more of a.......

Yes, I think of myself more as an orchestrator and an arranger. Composer somewhat. From extended now on I'll probably do more standard things. Most of the time my composition has been within another number. I may write a whole special ensemble chorus in another song you know, is my whole composition really.

That's when I woke up one day and realised I wasn't getting any royalties. (LAUGHTER). Hey, wait a minute! For a long time I had fun. I enjoyed arranging other people's music. Always stayed at home. But all of a sudden..........
(And when you add it up that's all you did have?). (LAUGHTER).
It doesn't work out so good twenty years later. I wasn't thinking about that. (LAUGHTER). I guess I'm a grasshopper and not an ant. (LAUGHTER).
